response.justification: Experienced, versatile senior engineer with genuine geospatial credentials (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS, FOSS4G talk) and some low-latency, high-throughput backend work (Sociomantic, millions of req/s in D). However, the role's primary hard requirement — modern C++ or Rust in commercial/open-source settings — is essentially unmet: the only C/C++ exposure is a ~7-month stint at National Instruments in 2014-2015 on a legacy C IDE, plus a university thesis project. The last decade is dominated by TypeScript/Node.js product work, with no Rust, no navigation/routing systems, and no evidence of routing tile pipelines or map data transformation at scale. Could be worth a conversation given the D-language systems background and geospatial domain interest, but they would be a significant ramp-up risk versus candidates with current C++ depth.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS domain experience across multiple projects
Low-latency, high-throughput distributed backend work in D
Strong testing/TDD culture and broad full-stack adaptability
concerns: No modern C++ or Rust experience in the last ~10 years
No navigation, routing, or map-tiling pipeline background
Recent roles are web/product TypeScript, not systems engineering
